title: The Horizon of the Empty Quarter
premise: Beatrix Galloway, a disgraced railroad engineer carrying a map of lines the company paid to erase, joins an expedition into the Empty Quarter after a low tide exposes a cave the Bedouin legends charge in blood to enter. Inside, the team finds evidence that the railroad's founders buried a massacre — and one of their own party was sent to make sure it stays buried. To bring everyone home alive, Beatrix must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the woman he loves, who works for the company that will kill to keep its secret. In the end he burns his map, smuggles the survivors out through closed rail lines only he can navigate, and mails the evidence to a newspaper from a border town neither of them will ever see again.
about_author: Mara Ishikawa is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years mapping desert rail corridors before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose professions are also their prisons.

chapters.title: The Tide That Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A freak tide drains a coastal lagoon and reveals a cave mouth carved with warnings no one can read. Beatrix, hired to survey 'closed' rail spurs nearby, recognizes the cave sits exactly where his erased map says nothing should be. Emotional beat: restless curiosity curdling into dread as he realizes someone wanted this coastline forgotten.

chapters.title: A Party of Convenient Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The expedition assembles: a company geologist, a journalist with too many questions, a guide named Halima who knows the old songs, and Elias Voss, the company man whose smile never reaches his eyes. Beatrix meets Elena Marsh, the geologist, and feels the first dangerous pull. Emotional beat: wary attraction shadowed by the sense that everyone here has been chosen for a reason.

chapters.title: Lines That Were Never Built
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Following his doctored map inland, Beatrix finds rail bed graded but never laid — a corridor built toward the cave and then abandoned overnight. Elena catches him studying it and asks the question he can't answer. Emotional beat: intimacy growing through shared suspicion; duty and desire pulling in opposite directions for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Songs Charge
chapters.summary: POV Halima. Halima translates the cave inscriptions: not a warning but a ledger — names of workers the railroad listed as 'lost to weather.' The legends demand admission because the mountain already took its price once. Voss quietly notes who reads what aloud. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the past stops being legend and becomes testimony.

chapters.title: The Chamber of Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Deep inside, the team finds a sealed chamber: company payrolls, telegrams ordering a tunnel collapse, and bones arranged by someone who wanted them counted. The journalist starts photographing. Voss 'accidentally' collapses the entrance behind them. Emotional beat: horror giving way to cold clarity — they were meant to find enough to stay quiet, not enough to speak.

chapters.title: Rations and Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Elena. Trapped with dwindling water, Elena counts supplies and realizes Voss brought exactly enough for fewer people than are present. She tells Beatrix without telling him — a look, a shifted canteen. Emotional beat: love declared sideways, in logistics instead of words, while trust becomes a survival resource scarcer than water.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix finds an air shaft on his old survey bearings and leads a split: some climb for help, others hold the chamber. The journalist goes with Voss's group and doesn't come back. Emotional beat: guilt hardening into resolve; Beatrix understands he isn't guiding an expedition anymore, he's running a rescue under a killer's nose.

chapters.title: Every Closed Line Has a Key
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. On the surface, Beatrix uses his forbidden knowledge of the closed spurs to route a supply train around Voss's telegraphed roadblocks. Halima buys them hours with misdirection; Elena forges a waybill. Emotional beat: justice outside the law — every rule broken tonight is a rule that protected the guilty first.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Sent Ahead
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Voss corners Beatrix at the last junction with a pistol and an offer: burn the photographs, keep Elena safe, retire rich. Beatrix answers by derailing the offer itself — Halima and the rescued climbers take Voss alive with his own confession recorded. Emotional beat: climax; loyalty to people finally outweighs fear of the institution that owns them all.

chapters.title: The Horizon of the Empty Quarter
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At a border station at dawn, Beatrix mails the ledgers and photographs to a newspaper, burns his map so no one else can be sent down those lines, and watches the empty quarter take back its silence. He and Elena board different trains on purpose — safer apart — each carrying half of everything true. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; love survives precisely because duty, at last, was chosen freely.
